top_signal.title: Need advice on how to implement price increases due to rising costs
top_signal.summary: I have a business where I design, manufacture, and sell small toy products. My business is entirely online, and my customer base is very very sensitive to price increases in general, as I've seen of their reactions to other companies doing so. The go to is to usually accuse the business of being greedy.    In the last year and a half, my manufacturing costs have risen more than 54% overall, with some key materials jumping more than 60% in price. I've been eating it. It's massively reduced my margins, but I was eating it hoping that things would balance out when I went debt free and paid off all my equipment earlier this year.    I did that, and then the Iran war happened and material costs jumped in June and again just recently, and now the savings from going debt free has almost completely disappeared.    I don't really have any choice now but to raise prices across the board.    How do I approach this with my customer base? Do I explain what's happened and why it's causing this, or do I just raise prices and say nothing?       submitted by     /u/DoubleJumps       [link]       [comments]
